about: Living Roots Wine & Co. was founded in 2016 by Sebastian and Colleen Hardy, and makes wine in two hemispheres. Seb comes from six generations of Australian winemakers: his great-great-great-grandfather Thomas Hardy arrived in South Australia in 1850 and planted some of its first vines. Colleen, a Rochester native who left marketing for the cellar, met him while working a vintage at Hardy’s Tintara winery. They make Finger Lakes wine at an urban winery in Rochester and red wines in the Adelaide Hills, and in 2023 Halliday’s Wine Companion named Living Roots Australia’s Best New Winery.

The Session wines are Living Roots’ lighter, lower-alcohol sparklers; the name borrows the brewer’s term for something you can enjoy over a long afternoon. For the rosé, mostly hybrid grapes from Finger Lakes vineyards are picked early to keep natural alcohol down. The wine is made sparkling in a pressurized tank (the Charmat method), using unfermented grape juice rather than added sugar to drive the second fermentation, which is stopped early to leave a balanced touch of sweetness.

The range also includes a Session Sparkling White made from old-vine Elvira, a native hybrid with roots in the Finger Lakes’ sparkling-wine tradition. For the rosé, the winemakers describe pretty florals, juicy fruit and refreshing acidity, and compare the palate, fondly, to a watermelon Jolly Rancher. The Beverage Testing Institute gave an early batch a Silver Medal, calling it dryish and suggesting it with fried chicken, chicken kebabs or a Cobb salad.
